newsitem.title: USA: Clinton approval down in one poll, stable in another.
newsitem.headline: Clinton approval down in one poll, stable in another.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's performance in office has dropped by six percentage points in one poll but remained steady in another one, according to surveys released on Tuesday
A Harris Poll showed Clinton's job approval rating dropped from 57 percent in February to 51 percent in a poll conducted March 27 through April 1.

A CBS News/New York Times Poll, however, showed Clinton's approval rating staying high at 56 percent between March and April, despite a rash of news stories about questionable campaign fund raising that has been dogging the White House.

In the Harris poll, approval ratings of Democrats in Congress were down four percentage points from 43 to 39 percent while approval ratings for congressioal Republicans dropped only one point from 38 to 37 percent.
The controversy over campaign financing abuses are hurting both parties, according to an analysis by Harris pollster Humphrey Taylor.

The Harris poll of 1,006 adults had a margin of error of three percentage points. The CBS News/New York Times poll was taken among 1,347 adullts on April 2-5 and had a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.
